title: The stop instruction halts immediately
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $w$ be a finite Boolean input, let $\rho$ assign a natural-number value to each of eleven registers, and let $p$ be a natural-number input position. Starting the associated counter program at its stop label with register assignment $\rho$, input position $p$, and any previously printed output, it halts in one step, leaving the registers and input position unchanged and appending no output.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols
An assignment of natural numbers to eleven registers
An arbitrary previously printed Boolean output
